task_objective: Replace the JSON-backed saved-query store with a directory of .sql files chosen in Preferences, after first assessing feasibility and cost.
user_decisions: description is the leading comment at the top of each query file
no migration of the existing saved_queries.json
defaults accepted: case-insensitive .sql suffix, explicit Refresh instead of a filesystem watcher
tests_added: test_saved_query_store.py: 12 functions covering recursive scan and sort, name derivation, case-insensitive suffix, dot-prefixed and undecodable exclusion, leading -- and /* */ description parsing, subfolder save, collision, name validation and traversal rejection, whitespace trimming, rename across subfolders, rename clobber refusal, delete, missing root, and atomic write
test_settings_service.py: saved-query directory round trip and blank-value fallback
test_file_dialog_service.py: choose_directory on the Qt service and the fake
test_saved_queries_dock.py: description filtering and tooltip, Refresh action signal, empty list for a missing directory

test_main_window.py: file-backed Open in New Tab overwritten by Save, delete confirmation honouring No then Yes, unusable-name status message, missing-folder report on Refresh, and Preferences folder change repointing the library
design_decisions: SavedQuery.id is the absolute file path and name is the POSIX-relative path without the suffix, so recursion needs no extra disambiguation and the dock's existing Qt.UserRole item identity keeps working unchanged.
created_at was dropped because no portable filesystem creation time exists; updated_at comes from st_mtime.
Case-insensitive name uniqueness was dropped: the filesystem now decides, and an explicit Path.exists() check reports collisions instead of silently overwriting.
Name validation rejects backslashes, NUL, absolute paths, empty, '.' and '..' components, and components ending in a space or a dot, then verifies the resolved path is inside the configured root.
SavedQueryDirectory.set_directory repoints one shared library object, so the dock needs no store-swapping API when the preference changes.
Writes go through the existing write_atomically helper rather than Path.write_text, so an interrupted save cannot truncate an existing query file.

The startup missing-folder status message was removed after it broke an unrelated close-behaviour test; the folder is reported only on Refresh, a Preferences change, or a failed save, and save_query creates the folder on demand.
verification: Feasibility probe before planning: drove the real SavedQueriesDock against a directory-backed stand-in under offscreen Qt, proving the widget needs no source change, that a file path works as the item id, and that a 500-file refresh costs 7.1 ms including reading every file (1.1 ms for a name-only scan).
./run.sh uv run ruff check . --fix: all checks passed
./run.sh uv run ruff format .: 207 files unchanged after formatting
./run.sh uv run ty check src/: all checks passed

End-to-end smoke test through the real MainWindow: recursive listing with case-insensitive suffix, comment-based tooltips and filtering, a real DuckDB run binding {dataset} to a quoted alias and :region to a bound value returning the two expected rows, file-backed tab overwritten by Save, rename into a new subfolder, delete refused then confirmed, traversal name rejected with a status message, and a missing folder reported on Refresh.
results: Complete. The Saved Queries dock now lists .sql files from a configurable folder, saved queries are editable as files, and Ctrl+S overwrites them. The old JSON store is gone with no migration, as requested.
unverified: No Windows verification; the reserved-name and trailing-dot rules are enforced defensively rather than tested on Windows.
The Preferences folder row was exercised through the fake dialog service and offscreen Qt, not through a native directory dialog.
Sync-client conflict files, such as 'query (conflicted copy).sql', will appear as ordinary saved queries; this is untested and accepted.
